g.text: One list, two ways to take
Swap the to-do list. What changes?
Same search: take a place, add its unseen neighbours.
One difference: take from the front, or the top.
Panels identical; no next-tile outline while locked.
B) The order places are visited
C) It no longer reaches every place
One list, two ways to take
Same search: take a place, add its unseen neighbours.
One difference: take from the front, or the top.
Queue took B (front). Stack took C (top).
One list, two ways to take
Same search: take a place, add its unseen neighbours.
One difference: take from the front, or the top.
Order: A B C D E F
Order: A C F E B D
Both lists reached all six places. The queue took
A B C D E F, ring by ring; the stack took A C F E B D,
going deep first. Same steps; only which waiting place
came next changed. E: queue 2 hops, stack 3.
Ring by ring is why breadth-first finds fewest-hop routes.
